gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.

gaps.sentence: 'OK, I'll help you move house,' she said. She ___ to help me move house.
gaps.explanation: Agreement to a request is reported as agreed to do something.

gaps.sentence: She ___ that she would be waiting by the main entrance.
gaps.hint: say takes no personal object here
gaps.explanation: Say (that)... without a personal object; 'told that' is impossible without the object.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).
